فتظهر لك في ذلك كله فتميله
items.lemma: كل ما كان من الأسماء والأفعال من ذوات الياء

forms.desc: يميلون كل ما كان من الأسماء والأفعال من ذوات الياء

items.note: The imāla of nouns and verbs that end in an alif written as a yāʾ (موسى, الهدى, أبى), and of those from a wāw that are heard with a yāʾ when a letter is added. The five words حتى, لدى, إلى, على and ما زكى are read with a fatḥa by agreement. The book gives the test of turning the noun into a dual or the verb to the speaker's form.
items.chapter: باب ذكر الفتح والإمالة وبين اللفظين

ev: وقرأ أبو عمرو ما كان من جميع ما تقدم
items.lemma: أبو عمرو ما كان من جميع ما تقدم
items.note: Abū ʿAmr: the imāla where a rāʾ comes before the alif, and between the two in the ends of verses in suras whose verses end in a yāʾ or hāʾ-alif, and in the weights فعلى, فعلى, فعلى; a fatḥa in the rest.
items.chapter: باب ذكر الفتح والإمالة وبين اللفظين

ev: وقرأ ورش جميع ذلك بين اللفظين
items.note: Warsh reads all of it between the two, except in suras whose verse endings are a hāʾ-alif, where he gives a pure fatḥa on a disputed report. The author read the pure fatḥa to Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Ghalbūn and between the two to Ibn Khāqān and Abū al-Fatḥ. He says the rāʾ words have their own rule.

items.note: Shuʿba: رمى in al-Anfāl and أعمى in the two places of al-Isrāʾ. Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb follow him on the first أعمى only.

items.lemma: واتفق مع حمزة وخلف على الإمالة
items.note: Where al-Kisāʾī agrees with Ḥamza and Khalaf: ويحيى and أحيا joined with a wāw, الدنيا and العليا and others. Hishām follows on إناه only. The author adds that al-Kisāʾī agrees with Khalaf on الرؤيا with the article.

وتابعهما خلف على إمالة [شاء وجاء] حيث وقعا

items.note: Ten verbs: جاء, شاء, زاد, خاف, طاب, خاب, ران, حاق, ضاق, and زاغ. Ibn Dhakwān follows on شاء and جاء and on فزادهم in the start of al-Baqara, on the report of Ibn al-Akhram from al-Akhfash; others report the imāla everywhere. Khalaf adds شاء and جاء.

items.note: Ḥamza: the imāla of the hamza in أنا آتيك به (the two places in al-Naml) and of the ʿayn in ضعافا. The book says there is a difference for Khallād in these three, and the author takes the fatḥa for him.

forms.desc: وتابعه حمزة على ما كان من ذلك الراء فيه مكررة

items.note: An alif before a rāʾ with a kasra that is the last letter of the word (النار, أبصارهم, بقنطار). Abū al-Ḥārith and Khalaf take only the words with a doubled rāʾ. Warsh reads all between the two; Ḥamza follows him on the doubled-rāʾ words, القهار and دار البوار. Ibn Dhakwān, from the author's reading to Fāris and al-Fārisī: إلى حمارك and الحمار in al-Baqara and al-Jumuʿa only.

items.note: The book gives this as the narration of al-Dūrī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū Ḥamdūn and Ibn Saʿdān from al-Yazīdī; another route from al-Yazīdī gives the fatḥa, which Ibn Mujāhid took.

ev: وسيأتي بعد إن شاء الله تعالى

desc: بإمالة الراء من المحراب حيث وقع فقط

items.note: Hishām alone: ومشارب in Yā Sīn, من عين آنية in al-Ghāshiya, and عابدون/عابد in al-Kāfirūn. Ibn Dhakwān has three routes for the imāla of the rāʾ (from the author's reading to Abū al-Fatḥ, to al-Fārisī from al-Naqqāsh, and to Abū al-Ḥasan). The book says the rest give a pure fatḥa, except for Warsh's rules on the rāʾ.

items.note: Al-Kisāʾī, on stopping on the feminine hāʾ and its like: the imāla of the letter before it, except after one of ten letters (ṭāʾ, ẓāʾ, ṣād, ḍād, khāʾ, ghayn, qāf, alif, ḥāʾ, ʿayn), with further conditions for the rāʾ, the hamza, the hāʾ and the kāf. The teachers differ; the author follows the analogy of the route of the book.
